{{Quote|Get on the ''quad guns'' and hold them off until I make the jump to ''lightspeed''!|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], to [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]|<ref name="My Spaceship">{{SWComicCite|7.7|My Spaceship, My Enemy}}</ref>}}
The [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] '''AG-2G quad laser cannon''' was a powerful [[Quad laser cannon/Legends|quad laser cannon]], two of which were installed on the top and bottom of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] by [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and modified by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], the latter of whom also added the ventral cannons. [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Lancer-class frigate/Legends|''Lancer''-class frigates]] mounted twenty of these quad [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]], for use against fast-moving starfighters.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>

==Description==
[[File:AG2GQuadLaserCannon-SWBTUC.jpg|thumb|left|180px|AG-2G schematics]]
The cannons drew power directly from the ''Falcon''{{'s}} [[Quadex/Legends|Quadex]] power core. Enhanced [[power cycler]]s, high-volume [[gas feed]]s, and custom-modified [[Laser actuator/Legends|laser actuators]] (with larger [[Energization crystal/Legends|energization crystals]]) greatly increased the cannon's energy output, and the weapon could destroy a [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighter]] with a single shot. Enhanced cooling packs and compressors allowed for prolonged fire without the risk of overheating. The splitter coupling dispersed the energy beam, forcing the target's shields to deflect energy simultaneously from two hits and increasing the likelihood of overloading the shields and inflicting greater damage. The laser barrels fired one blast at a time, following a rotation by the gunner, and had a rate of fire of 1.32 seconds for each barrel.<ref name="Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 1">[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 1|''Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon'' 1]]</ref>

The turret utilized pedals for the gunner to rotate the gun left or right, and vertical control sticks to move up or down. The turret could automatically rotate via the use of a ball-swivel rotation mounting and via the commands of the tactical [[Targeting computer/Legends|targeting computer]].

The cannon's main control area was accessible via ladders and access tubes. In front of the gunner's seat were the main controls, which included twin firing grips with built-in triggers. The tactical targeting computer was slightly beyond the main controls. Several dials and buttons on the left wall constituted the system status indicators. A maintenance access panel was nearby. The viewports were made of [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]], and the directional control pedals were located near the viewport. Below the floor was the rotating platform base. The cannon itself featured a horizontal support arm, four laser barrels, tracking servos on top of the turret, a laser cooling unit near the top two barrels, and the swivel mount near the bottom half, which was connected to the horizontal support arms. The cannon's targeting computers were designed to augment the gunner's skills, were accurate up to the longest range of the weapon, and could lock on to any target greater than four meters in length that stayed within scanning range for more than 1.5 seconds. However, this was ineffective against most Imperial TIE models.

The position of the cannons on the ''Falcon'', combined with its overall design, caused their line of fire to converge into a wedge all the way around the ship. Thus, Solo and Chewbacca often held standing wagers on who was the better shot with the quad cannons, with kills scored in this area&mdash;dubbed the Money Lane&mdash;carrying a double payoff.

The cannons could also be activated by remote control, and avoided hitting the pilot via a transponder. When Calrissian had the ship, the remote control was via auxiliary foot pedals in the cockpit. Solo installed trackball controllers to replace these pedals, due to their awkward design and Chewbacca's need for legroom.
